From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Anna Reed <anna.reed@greyhoundcapital.com>, Tom Sullivan <tom.sullivan@seedbridge.vc>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stakeholder slidebook: final edit cycle + OKR alignment

Team —

Attaching v3 of the stakeholder slidebook and the Q3 financials workbook. This is the last edit cycle before we share with the board/investors next week. High-level asks: 

- Narrative: please review the top-line framing on slide 2 (market positioning + product momentum). If you have language suggestions, paste the line under my comment on the Drive link.
- OKRs: slide 6 should reflect the updated metrics we discussed; Karthik, please confirm numbers.
- Financials: slide 10 needs the updated ARR bridge and customer logo callouts. Markus, I’ve left your earlier notes as comments but flagged a few hard numbers we should tighten.
- Appendix: add one slide with Q&A bullets and one appendix row with SOC2/compliance status.

Deadline: EOD Friday 9/8 PT for any changes. If you can’t hit that, reply with the exact section you can review by Thursday. Plan: finalize Friday evening, and I’ll schedule a 30-min dry run early Monday 9/11 before investor distribution.

Attachments: Q3_stakeholder_slidebook_v3.pptx (slidebook), financials_Q3.xlsx (backup figures)

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
VP, GTM Strategy & Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Anna Reed <anna.reed@greyhoundcapital.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder slidebook: final edit cycle + OKR alignment

Thanks, Soojin — I skimmed v3 and added inline comments on Drive. High-level:

- Slide 2 (narrative): tighten the opening paragraph. Suggest: “Redwood is delivering consistent latency wins while lowering inference unit costs for production customers — enabling new ML features at scale.”
- Slide 6 (OKRs): move the ‘Model catalog expansion’ item into the product slide; it’s diluting the go-to-market focus.
- Slide 10 (financials): the ARR bridge looks good but please avoid projecting >40% growth in the public slide without a clear FY guidance note. We can show the midpoint but flag assumptions in the appendix.

Inline comments include a couple of small copy edits. I can take a pass on the narrative tomorrow morning and return a clean paragraph for slide 2.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Chief Customer Officer
Redwood Inference

Soojin / team —

I made a few adjustments to the financials and attached a cleaned workbook (financials_Q3_revised.xlsx). Key changes:

- Updated ARR bridge to reflect the Q2 carryover corrections (see tab 'ARR_bridge'). Net effect: ~2.3% lower 'net new ARR' vs the draft, mostly timing.
- Reduced the FY24 projection callout to a range (35–38%) and added the assumptions footnote we discussed (largest contributors: enterprise renewals and Dedicated booking cadence).
- Moved the customer logo slide later in the deck and removed one logo flagged as not yet approved for public use.

I also inserted a separate spreadsheet tab with sensitivity runs. Happy to review redlines with finance tomorrow if useful.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Finance
Redwood Inference

All — quick OKR data updates attached (OKR_summary_2026_Q3.csv). Notes: 

- Slide 6: updated ARR expansion metric to 12% (was 10%), updated trial-to-paid conversion to 18% (slide label and footnote).
- Added a one-line callout for model performance improvements tied to the serving runtime optimizations (suggested language: “Serving runtime improvements reduced median inference latency by 28% for our top-10 customer workloads”).

If nobody flags these changes by EOD Thursday (9/8), assume OK to land.

Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder slidebook: final edit cycle + OKR alignment

Soojin — thanks for looping us in and for the clear deck. A couple of small external-facing notes from our side: 

- On the ARR slide, it’d be helpful to show a single-sentence assumption for the growth range (e.g., booking cadence + renewals) rather than more granular sensitivity tables — that makes the narrative cleaner for limited time board reads.
- Consider removing the term “aggressive” in public materials — phrase it as “ambitious” or cite the specific operational levers enabling the target.
- Customer logos: great to have, but show the two logos that best represent cross-industry adoption (SaaS + e-comm) rather than a broader tile.

Happy to take a quick call if you want to talk through the narrative. Looking forward to the final.

Anna Reed
Partner
Greyhound Capital

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Stakeholder slidebook: final edit cycle + OKR alignment

Thanks, everyone — and thanks Anna for the external POV. I reviewed the collated comments and we’re in good shape to finalize. Final checklist (to close by EOD 9/8):

1) Soojin: incorporate Laura’s narrative paragraph for slide 2 and Karthik’s updated OKR numbers.
2) Markus: land the revised financials and remove the unapproved logo.
3) Soojin/Laura: update ARR slide language per Anna’s suggestion (range + single-sentence assumption).
4) Logistics: I will schedule the 30-min dry run for Mon 9/11 at 9:30am PT and invite the investor reps.

If anyone has a blocker, flag it now — otherwise mark this approved from leadership. I’ll take the final after Soojin uploads v4 to Drive and send the external distribution.

Jonas Weber
Head of GTM Operations (interim)
Redwood Inference
